content.question: Who wrote Harshacharita, the biography of Harshavardhana?
content.note: Banbhatta was the Asthana Kavi (Court Poet) of King Harshavardhana. He wrote the Harshacharita, which is the first historical biography in Sanskrit, detailing the rise of the Pushyabhuti dynasty. He also authored Kadambari, one of the world's earliest novels.

content.question: Who established Vikramashila University and revived Nalanda University?
content.note: Dharmapala, the second ruler of the Pala Dynasty, was a great patron of Buddhism. He established Vikramashila University in Bihar to maintain the quality of Buddhist education and granted 200 villages to revive Nalanda University.

content.question: Which is the only Indus Valley site with an artificial brick dockyard?
content.note: Lothal is famous for being the world's earliest known artificial dockyard, connecting the city to an ancient course of the Sabarmati river. This site proves the maritime trade capabilities of the Indus Valley Civilization with Mesopotamia.

content.question: During whose reign did Hieun Tsang visit India?
content.note: The Chinese pilgrim Hieun Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India to study Buddhist texts at Nalanda. Harshavardhana held a grand assembly at Kannauj in his honor. He is often called the 'Prince of Pilgrims'.

content.question: Who was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title Maharajadhiraja?
content.note: While his predecessors used the title Maharaja, Chandragupta I was the first to adopt Maharajadhiraja ('King of Kings'), signaling the rise of the imperial power of the Gupta Empire around 319-320 CE.

content.question: Who composed the Sanskrit grammar treatise Ashtadhyayi?
content.note: Panini was an ancient Sanskrit philologist and grammarian. His work, Ashtadhyayi, is a foundational text of Vyakarana (linguistics), consisting of eight chapters and roughly 4,000 rules (sutras).

content.question: Where did Buddha deliver his first sermon Dharmachakrapravartan?
content.note: After attaining enlightenment, Gautam Buddha traveled to Sarnath (near Varanasi) where he gave his first sermon to five disciples. This event is symbolically known as Dharmachakrapravartan or 'Turning the Wheel of Law'.

content.question: Which Mauryan ruler fought the Kalinga War in 261 BCE?
content.note: The Kalinga War was a turning point for Ashoka. Moved by the immense bloodshed and suffering, he abandoned Digvijaya (conquest by force) for Dhammavijaya (conquest by piety) and embraced Buddhism.

content.question: King Kanishka belonged to which dynasty?
content.note: Kanishka was the most powerful ruler of the Kushan Dynasty. He is famous for convening the 4th Buddhist Council in Kashmir and starting the Saka Era in 78 CE, which is used by the Indian government today.

content.question: Who wrote Indica describing Mauryan India?
content.note: Megasthenes was a Greek ethnographer and ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator. His book Indica provided a detailed account of the Mauryan administration, military, and social classes, though the original text is lost.

content.question: Megasthenes visited the court of which Mauryan emperor?
content.note: Megasthenes stayed at the Mauryan capital, Pataliputra, during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya. He described the king’s lifestyle and the efficiency of the municipal administration.

content.question: Where did Gautam Buddha attain enlightenment?
content.note: Gautam Buddha attained Nirvana (Enlightenment) at the age of 35 under a Peepal tree (the Bodhi Tree) on the banks of the Falgu River in Bodh Gaya, Bihar.

content.question: Gautamiputra Shatakarni was a ruler of which dynasty?
content.note: Gautamiputra Shatakarni was the greatest ruler of the Satavahana Dynasty. He is described in the Nasik Prashasti as the 'destroyer of Shakas' and the 'unique Brahmana'.

content.question: Where was the Great Bath found?
content.note: The Great Bath is the most significant structure found at Mohenjo-daro. It was a large rectangular tank used for ritual bathing, showcasing the advanced engineering and urban planning of the Harappans.

content.question: Who founded Nalanda University?
content.note: Nalanda University, a world-renowned center of higher learning in ancient Magadha, was founded by the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I in the 5th century CE.

content.question: Rajaraja I belonged to which dynasty?
content.note: Rajaraja I was a formidable king of the Chola Dynasty. He built the magnificent Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur and expanded Chola influence over Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

content.question: During whose reign was the Great Stupa at Sanchi built?
content.note: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, located in Madhya Pradesh, was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka the Great in the 3rd century BCE to house the relics of Lord Buddha.

content.question: Which dynasty built the Khajuraho temples?
content.note: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments, famous for its Nagara-style architecture and erotic sculptures, was built between 950 and 1050 CE by the Chandela Dynasty.

content.question: What is the Greco-Roman Buddhist art school known as?
content.note: Gandhara Art developed in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent. It is a fusion of Greek, Roman, and Buddhist influences, characterized by realistic human figures and flowing drapery on Buddha statues.

content.question: Which three dynasties were involved in the Tripartite Struggle?
content.note: The Tripartite Struggle was a long-running conflict between the Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas of Malwa, and the Rashtrakutas of Deccan for control over the strategic city of Kannauj.

content.question: What was the capital of the Pallava dynasty?
content.note: Kanchipuram (Kanchi) served as the capital of the Pallava Dynasty. It became a major center of learning and Dravidian architecture, famous for its shore temples and rock-cut shrines.

content.question: Who founded the Shunga dynasty?
content.note: Pushyamitra Shunga was the commander-in-chief of the last Mauryan King, Brihadratha. He assassinated the king and founded the Shunga Dynasty around 185 BCE.

content.question: Where is Dholavira located?
content.note: Dholavira is an Indus Valley site located on Khadir Bet in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. It is unique for its sophisticated water management system and division into three parts (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town).

content.question: Where was Gautam Buddha born?
content.note: Gautam Buddha was born as Prince Siddhartha in the royal gardens of Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) to King Suddhodana and Queen Maya around 563 BCE.

content.question: What is the meaning of Mohenjo-daro?
content.note: The name Mohenjo-daro translates to 'Mound of the Dead' in the Sindhi language. It was one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.

content.question: Which Harappan site shows evidence of ploughing?
content.note: Kalibangan, located in Rajasthan, provides the earliest archaeological evidence of a ploughed agricultural field. It is also known for its unique fire altars.

content.question: Where was a terracotta plough found?
content.note: While Kalibangan showed a field, a terracotta model of a plough was specifically discovered at Banawali in the Hisar district of Haryana.

content.question: What is Bhimbetka famous for?
content.note: Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its prehistoric rock shelters and paintings that date back to the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods.

content.question: Which Indus Valley site is located in Pakistan?
content.note: Harappa, the first site of the civilization to be excavated (1921), is located in the Punjab province of Pakistan on the old bank of the River Ravi.

content.question: What was the real name of Buddha?
content.note: The real name of the Buddha was Siddhartha Gautama. He was a prince of the Sakya clan of Kapilvastu before he renounced his worldly life.

content.question: At what age did Lord Mahavir leave home in search of knowledge?
content.note: At the age of thirty, Vardhamana Mahavira (the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism) renounced his princely life and family to live as an ascetic in search of spiritual truth.

content.question: What was the shape of the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro?
content.note: The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro was rectangular in shape. It measured approximately 12 meters by 7 meters, with a depth of 2.4 meters, featuring brick-lined walls and a bitumen coating for waterproofing.

content.question: At which site has evidence of millet cultivation been found in ancient India?
content.note: Hallur, located in Karnataka, is a Neolithic-Megalithic site where archaeologists discovered charred grains, providing early evidence of millet cultivation in South India.

content.question: In which state is the prehistoric site Daimabad located?
content.note: Daimabad is a Chalcolithic archaeological site located on the banks of the Pravara River in Maharashtra. It is famous for its exquisite bronze figurines, including a chariot.

content.question: Fire altars have been found in which Harappan sites?
content.note: Ritual fire altars (Havankunda) have been discovered at Kalibangan (Rajasthan) and Lothal (Gujarat), suggesting that the Harappans performed sacrificial or religious fire rituals.

content.question: Which material was primarily used for Harappan seals?
content.note: While many materials were used, the majority of Harappan seals were made from Steatite (soapstone), though Terracotta (baked clay) was widely used for toys and figurines.

content.question: Which part of Harappan cities was known as the Lower Town?
content.note: Harappan cities were usually divided into two parts: the Citadel (Western, higher) and the Lower Town (Eastern part, lower but larger), where the common citizens lived.

content.question: Which metal was used to make tools and weapons in Harappan cities?
content.note: The Harappans were in the Bronze Age. They primarily used Copper and its alloy, Bronze (copper + tin), to manufacture tools, weapons, and statues.

content.question: Who discovered the Harappa site of the Indus Valley Civilization?
content.note: In 1921, Rai Bahadur Daya Ram Sahni led the excavation that discovered the ruins of Harappa, the first site of the Indus Valley Civilization to be identified.

content.question: Which site of the Indus Valley Civilization was located on the banks of the Luni River?
content.note: Dholavira is located on Khadir Bet in the Rann of Kutch and was situated near the now-dry bed of the Luni River. It is famous for its unique water harvesting systems.

content.question: Which archaeological site is significant in Jammu and Kashmir?
content.note: Burzahom is a significant Neolithic site in the Kashmir Valley. It is well-known for its unique pit-dwellings (houses dug into the ground) and distinctive burial practices.

content.question: Which is the oldest stupa from the Buddhist period?
content.note: The Sanchi Stupa is regarded as the oldest stone structure in India. Originally commissioned by Ashoka, it was later expanded and encased in stone by the Shunga dynasty.

content.question: During whose reign did Buddhism split into Mahayana and Hinayana?
content.note: During the 4th Buddhist Council held in Kashmir under the patronage of King Kanishka, Buddhism split into two major sects: Mahayana (Great Vehicle) and Hinayana (Lesser Vehicle).

content.question: In which language were ancient Buddhist texts written?
content.note: Most of the Tripitakas and early Buddhist scriptures were written in Pali, a Middle Indo-Aryan language that was the common tongue of the people during Buddha's time.

content.question: How many phases are there in the Paleolithic Age in India?
content.note: The Indian Paleolithic Age (Old Stone Age) is divided into three phases: Lower Paleolithic, Middle Paleolithic, and Upper Paleolithic, based on the types of stone tools used.

content.question: What was the main social unit of the Aryans?
content.note: The Jan (Tribe) was the highest social and political unit of the Early Vedic Aryans. The leader of the Jan was called the Rajan, who protected the people and their cattle.
